;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[August 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***At least four people are killed and another six injured by a [[roadside bomb]] exploding in [[Panjwayi District]], [[Kandahar Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/four-civilians-killed-kandahar-roadside-mine-blast-0 (TOLOnews)]

;Business and economy
*[[Apple Inc. litigation]], [[Google litigation]]
**[[Epic Games]] sues both [[Apple Inc.]] and [[Google]] in an [[antitrust]] case after the removal of ''[[Fortnite]]'' from the [[App Store (iOS)|Apple App Store]] and [[Google Play]] earlier in the day, alleging that the two companies hold an unfair [[monopoly]] over development for their respective ecosystems. The game was removed for implementing a feature allowing Epic to directly sell [[microtransactions]] while bypassing the 30% cut imposed on developers per transaction by both Apple and Google. [https://www.theverge.com/2020/8/13/21367963/epic-fortnite-legal-complaint-apple-ios-app-store-removal-injunctive-relief (''The Verge'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****The number of new [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases in India rises by nearly 67,000, a record high since the pandemic began. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/record-single-day-spike-of-66-999-cases-takes-india-s-covid-19-tally-to-nearly-2-4-million/story-rl8exHub58164hDzTwyDiK.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]]
****[[Iraq]] reports the highest single-day increase of over 3,800 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1718911/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
***[[Spain]] reports 2,935 new COVID-19 cases in the last 24 hours, which is the highest number of new cases since the lockdown was lifted in June. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-spain/spains-new-coronavirus-cases-spike-to-2935-total-at-337334-idUSKCN2592DQ (Reuters)]
***[[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] bans smoking in public places over concerns that it increases the risk of COVID-19 transmission. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53763267 (BBC News)]
***The [[Canary Islands]] also intend to ban outdoor smoking when [[social distancing]] cannot be guaranteed to prevent the spread of COVID-19. The smoking ban will take effect tomorrow, and wearing face masks will be mandatory in all public spaces. [https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2020/0813/1159030-canary-islands-smoking-ban/ (RTÉ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
***With 12 deaths, Venezuela reports its deadliest day since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://www.efe.com/efe/america/politica/mueren-12-personas-por-covid-19-en-el-dia-mas-negro-de-la-pandemia-venezuela/20000035-4319054 (EFE)]
***Governor of [[Capital District (Venezuela)|Capital District]] [[Darío Vivas]] dies from COVID-19. [https://www.elconfidencial.com/mundo/2020-08-14/dario-vivas-venezuela-coronavirus_2713928/ (''El Confidencial'')]

;International relations
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] imposes a two-week quarantine for travellers or people coming from [[France]] and the [[Netherlands]], as well as [[Monaco]], [[Malta]], [[Turks and Caicos]], and [[Aruba]]. The measure will take effect on 04:00 [[British Summer Time|BST]] on Saturday, August 15. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-53773914 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Ministry of Health (Italy)|Italian Health Minister]] [[Roberto Speranza]] signs an order requiring anyone arriving from [[Croatia]], [[Greece]], [[Spain]], and Malta to be tested for COVID-19 in an attempt to avoid a spike of new cases in the country. The country is also banning travellers from [[Colombia]] over concerns of new infections. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/italy-orders-covid-tests-on-travellers-from-greece--spain--croatia--malta/45964418 (Swiss Info)] [https://www.euronews.com/2020/08/13/italy-introduces-mandatory-covid-19-testing-for-tourists-returning-from-summer-holidays (Euronews)]
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**The Saudi ambassador to the [[United Nations]], Abdul Aziz al-Wasel, calls for an extension of the arms embargo on [[Iran]] saying that Iran "smuggles weapons to militias to disturb the peace in the Middle East". [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/gulf/2020/08/13/Saudi-Arabian-ambassador-to-Switzerland-calls-for-Iran-arms-embargo-extension.html (Al Arabiya)]
*[[Hezbollah foreign relations]]
**[[Lithuania]] labels [[Hezbollah]] a [[terrorist organization]] and bans its members from entering the country, according to a statement by the office of the foreign minister. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/08/13/Lithuania-recognizes-Hezbollah-as-terrorist-organization-after-Beirut-explosion.html (Al Arabiya)]
*[[Greek–Turkish relations]]
**[[France]] deploys two [[Dassault Rafale]] fighter jets and the [[French frigate La Fayette|frigate ''La Fayette'']] to the eastern Mediterranean because of tensions between Greece and Turkey over oil and gas exploration in disputed waters. French President [[Emmanuel Macron]] says the French military will monitor the situation. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53767792 (BBC News)]
*[[Foreign relations of Israel]], [[Arab–Israeli peace projects]]
**The [[United States]], [[Israel]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]] announce in a joint statement that Israel and the UAE will establish normalized diplomatic relations, in exchange for Israeli suspension of plans to annex [[occupied West Bank]] territory. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53770859 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (U.S. state)|COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia]]
***[[Governor of Georgia|Georgia Governor]] [[Brian Kemp]] drops his lawsuit against [[List of mayors of Atlanta|Atlanta Mayor]] [[Keisha Lance Bottoms]] over the city's mask mandate. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/georgia-governor-drop-lawsuit-atlanta-mask-mandate-72355332 (ABC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**A 25-year-old man from the city of [[Gomel]] becomes the second protester killed since protests in [[Belarus]] against the [[government of Belarus|government]] began. He died while in [[Militsiya (Belarus)|police]] custody, according to his family. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/aug/13/belarus-protests-25-year-old-man-dies-in-police-custody-alexander-vikhor (''The Guardian'')]
**The [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|UN High Commissioner for Human Rights]] [[Michelle Bachelet]] condemns the use of violence by Belarusian authorities against protesters, and calls for the release of all [[political prisoner]]s in the country. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53760453 (BBC News)] 
**[[Belarusians|Belarusian]] women form human chains to condemn a crackdown on protests over the disputed election. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53761747 (BBC News)]
**Factory workers from state-run factories joined the protest. Tens of thousands of people protested for the fifth day in a row against the election results. The protesters marched through [[Minsk]] and formed human chains. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election/go-away-state-factory-workers-join-protests-against-belarus-president-idUSKCN25925Z?feedType=mktg&feedName=topNews&WT.mc_id=Partner-Google (Reuters)]
*[[2019–2020 Lebanese protests]], aftermath of the [[2020 Beirut explosions]]
**[[parliament of Lebanon|Parliament]] approves a [[state of emergency]] in [[Beirut]] and grants the [[Lebanese Armed Forces|military]] sweeping powers, such as declaring [[curfew]]s, preventing public gatherings and [[Censorship|censoring]] the media, as well as referring civilians to military courts over alleged security breaches. [[Human rights in Lebanon|Human rights]] groups criticize the decision. [https://apnews.com/4434959ad39d1f2f189eb6442d590930 (AP)]
*[[2020 Bolivian general election]]
**The interim [[government of Bolivia]] confirms that the elections will be held on October 18. Anyone who tries to change the date may face penalties. Opposition parties called to have the elections sooner after the elections earlier this year were postponed because of [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia|COVID-19]]. Protesters have blocked streets and protested calling for the elections to take place sooner, after it was announced in July. The [[European Union]] and [[United Nations]] support the new election date. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-election-protest/bolivia-confirms-presidential-election-for-october-18-despite-calls-for-earlier-date-idUSKCN25A015 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of North Korea]]
**[[Kim Tok-hun]] is named the new [[Premier of North Korea|Premier]], succeeding [[Kim Jae-ryong]]. [https://www.shine.cn/news/world/2008144147/ (Shine)]
